title: Create isolated tfstate shards and GPU affinity adapter for tenant-scoped networking
author: Alyssa Tang
release_notes: Add tenant-scoped tfstate shards and a GPU affinity adapter controller to isolate state and improve subnet/GPU binding. Includes a migration helper and Helm hooks. No breaking API changes; operator upgrade required.
commits: init: add tfstate-sharder module and user guide
feat: implement gpu-affinity-adapter controller and Helm chart changes
chore: installer bootstrap accepts shard mapping and shard keys
migrate: migration helper script to split existing tfstate into tenant shards
fix: IAM aliasing for cross-tenant role links
test: add unit and e2e harness for adapter and migration path
review_comments: Marcus Lee (request changes): Rollback safety is my main concern. If migration partially succeeds we could end up with half the tenant pointing at a new shard and the installer still referencing the old one. Suggest a checkpointing file and an idempotent rollback. -- Alyssa: added checkpointing to migrate_shards.py, introduced a validation pass before switch-over, and documented the rollback steps in tfstate-sharding.md.

Priya Shah (comment): Can the affinity adapter handle multi-AZ clusters with mixed GPU types? Please ensure scheduling doesn't cause cross-AZ traffic for low-latency workloads. -- Alyssa: adapter now prefers same-AZ subnets and falls back to compatible GPU types only when allowed by a new "relax_affinity" flag. Documented behaviour in README.

Diego Alvarez (approve): Verified e2e tests in the canary cluster and checked IAM role creation. Small nit: rename shard_key -> shard_id in variables for clarity. -- Alyssa: renamed the variable and updated all references.
CI Bot (status): First pipeline failed (lint) on helm chart indentation. Re-run fixed after chart tweak. All checks green on final run.
description:
Background: Private installs historically used a single global tfstate for networking and GPU nodepools. That has been a scaling and blast-radius problem: a single tfstate edit can impact multiple tenants and complicates network isolation rollouts. This PR introduces a tenant-scoped tfstate sharding approach plus a runtime GPU affinity adapter that binds GPU nodepools to tenant subnets with stronger isolation guarantees. Motivation: 1) limit blast radius when changing subnet/GPU allocations; 2) enable per-tenant lifecycle (apply/rollback) for network and GPU resources; 3) simplify cross-tenant IAM scoping by isolating role bindings.

What this PR changes (summary): - terraform/modules/tfstate-sharder: new module that provides state backend mapping utilities and outputs a shard mapping manifest used by the installer. Supports S3/GCS backends with prefix-based shard keys. Includes README and usage examples. - installer bootstrap: bootstrapping code (cmd/installer/bootstrap/shard-mapper.go) now reads a shard mapping file and wires Terraform runs to the appropriate backend per-tenant. - GPU affinity adapter: a small controller deployed via Helm (helm/charts/installer/templates/gpu-affinity-adapter-deployment.yaml) that watches TenantSubnetClaim CRDs and ensures GPU nodepool labels/taints and subnet annotations reflect affinity rules. The controller is intentionally permissive by default; an operator flag enforces strict AZ-local affinity. - Migration helper: install-scripts/tfstate-migrator/migrate_shards.py provides a safe migration path from monolithic state to tenant shards. It performs a dry-run validation, writes a checkpoint file, copies state objects, validates resource IDs, and flips the mapping only after all checks pass. - IAM adjustments: modules/iam/tenant-roles.tf adds aliasing support to allow tenant-scoped roles to reference shared infra without granting global privileges.

Migration plan (high level): 1) run migration helper in dry-run mode against a snapshot; 2) run migration helper with --checkpoint-dir to create per-tenant state files and a checkpoint; 3) run installer in "drain-and-verify" mode (added flag) that verifies the shard mapping and performs a canary apply for 2 tenants; 4) if canary passes, flip the global mapping in the installer config and allow gradual rollout. Rollback: the migrator creates snapshot checkpoints and a manifest of moved resources so the installer can rebind original state if needed. See docs/private/tfstate-sharding.md for runbook.

Testing done: - unit tests for tfstate-sharder module validation and variable handling. - local e2e that spins up a 3-node cluster, provisions two tenant subnets, runs migrator, and exercises GPU affinity adapter (tests/e2e/gpu-affinity-migration.test.js). - CI: lint/format on terraform and helm, unit tests, and a smoke e2e harness (first run failed on helm lint; fixed and re-run).

Risk and mitigations: - Partial migration could result in split references: mitigated by checkpointing, pre-validation, and a reversible flip step. - Scheduler / cross-AZ traffic: adapter prefers same-AZ and can be toggled via values.yaml. - IAM regressions: IAM changes are additive; roles are created per-tenant and aliased rather than replacing global roles.

Operational notes: - Installer must be upgraded to >= v0.12.0 to honor shard mapping. - New Helm chart values: installer.gpuAffinity.strictAZ (default: false), installer.sharding.mappingPath. - Terraform state backends supported: S3 (recommended), GCS. - Rolling upgrade sequence is documented in docs/private/tfstate-sharding.md.

Checklist: - [x] Add tfstate-sharder module and docs - [x] Implement gpu-affinity-adapter and Helm hooks - [x] Add migration helper and checkpointing - [x] Unit and e2e tests - [x] Update installer bootstrap to read shard mapping - [x] Update docs and runbook

Related: Linear ENG-1423 (state partitioning), ENG-1487 (gpu affinity), SUP-621 (customer incident that spurred this work).
